name: Rel
tagline: Desktop 'true relational' DBMS implementing Date and Darwen's Tutorial D, for teaching and prototyping.
description: Rel is Dave Voorhis' open-source implementation of Tutorial D, the language C. J. Date and Hugh Darwen defined in The Third Manifesto to show what a truly relational database looks like: no NULLs, no duplicate tuples, relation-valued attributes, user-defined types and relvars instead of SQL tables. It is a zero-install Java desktop application with the DBrowser GUI, a visual query editor and a Berkeley DB Java Edition storage engine, and can also link CSV, Excel, Access and JDBC sources as relvars. It runs on Windows, macOS and Linux and is mostly used in courses on relational theory. The current release is 3.016 from 2022; the repository has only seen dependency updates since.
statusNote: Last release 3.016 (October 2022); since then only dependency bumps and minor commits.

scale.notes: A desktop and teaching DBMS; not designed for large or concurrent workloads.

strengths: Most complete runnable implementation of Tutorial D and The Third Manifesto
Strict relational semantics: no NULLs, no duplicates, relation-valued attributes
Zero-install desktop app with GUI and visual query editor
Can treat CSV, spreadsheets, Access and JDBC databases as relvars
weaknesses: Single maintainer; development has slowed to maintenance
Not built for production concurrency or large datasets
Tutorial D skills do not transfer directly to SQL jobs
useCases: Teaching relational theory and The Third Manifesto
Prototyping relational designs without SQL quirks
Personal desktop databases for relational purists
